cells.location: Āstakaṭṭi
cells.place: Stone set up to Chālu the northern side of the kya temple of Kalmēśvara of in the village.
cells.king: Regnal year 4, Saumya, Margasira, śu. 5, Monday= 1129 A.D., November 18.
cells.remarks: Refers to the Kadamba feudatory (Hangal) Tailapaš governorship over Banavāsa-1200 and Panungal-500. His feudatory Kētiṣeṭṭi is mentioned and his genealogy is given. The epigraph registers an endowment of 200 mattars of land and a house to god (probably Kalmēśvara) for worship and offerings such as nivēdya, gandha, dhūpa-di pa chaaitrapavitra khaṇḍaspuṭiṣ jīrṇōdhāra and for the food offerings of the ascetics (of the place). The boundaries are specified. The record was written by Chāvaṇṇa. The gift was made over after laying the feet of Bhadracharaṇa Pandiṭadēva. A few more grants are also mentioned.

cells.location: Muttagi
cells.place: Pedestal of Pārśvanātha idol recently excavated from the basement of A.N.M. Quarters.
cells.remarks: Records the installation of the idol of Pārśvanātha jointly by Tāṇya Ballana and Kochara Dombana in the basadi known as śinita-jinālaya of Muttaṭi. The above said donors were the disciples of Ravichandra-dēva, who in turn was the disciple of Ekavīra Paṇḍitadēva who seems to have belonged to Yapaniya-saṃgha, Kāraṇa-gaṇa and Mayilap-anvaya. Further it states that Uttamadēva of Uṇakal referred to as Ekkōṭi Chakravarti seems to have constructed a jinālaya at Ikkēśvara exclusively for the purpose of penance. In characters of the 10th century A.D.

cells.remarks: Eulogises Halla-gāvunḍa and others. Records that this temple of Śiva was constructed by Śānta-gāmunda and refers to Beṭṭa-gāvuṇḍa, a devoted servant (leŋka) of the king Jayakēśidēva. Further, it registers a grant of land by Halla-gāvunḍa for the food offerings and worship to the god. At the end, one more grant was made to the god Mūlasthānadēva free from all imposts by the same donor.

cells.place: (Bēchaṇāk)—Stone Kadamba Vīra Permmānādi- Regnal year Do. Gives an elaborate eulogy of king Jayakēśi, who is endowed
cells.dynasty: Śigatti—(Bēchaṇāk)—Stone Kadamba Vīra Permmānādi- Regnal year Do. Gives an elaborate eulogy of king Jayakēśi, who is endowed
cells.king: Regnal year 16, [Chitra] bhānu Puṣya ba. 2, Tuesday, Uttarāyana Sankrānti 1162 AD, December 25.
cells.remarks: Gives an elaborate eulogy of king Jayakēśi, who is endowed with epithets such as Śrīmat-sarvajñābharaṇa, tyāga-siṁhāsanam, rāya-piṭāmahaḥ, paścima-samudrādhiśvaram, and Konkaṇa-chakravarti. It states that king was ruling over Palasige-12000, Koriṁkaṇa-900 and Kavadadīpa-savakākka. His feudatory Jakkana son of Bammagavunda made a gift of land to the god Śūlāpāṇi. Further it states that the king Vīra-Permmādi granted lands to the god Siddheśvara for worship, khaṇḍasphuṭia-jīrṇōddhāra, Chaitra-Pavitra, etc. The royal family members (arasugalu) and gauṇḍas (local chiefs) were jointly made responsible for its protection. Further, his feudatory Nāṇayya-Nāyaka, who was also the mahāpradhāna and sādhi-vigrahika donated perpetual lamps and a few taxes such as bēravaṇa etc. At the end, the ayinūrvar also made a few more grants to the same god.

cells.location: KARNATAKA — Karnataka
cells.place: contd. DHARWAD DISTRICT—contd. KALGHATGI TALUK—contd. Sūllikatti.—Stone tablet lying in the premises of the dilapidated Rāma-liṅgēśvara temple.
cells.date: Śivachitta's regnal year [2]2, Sarvadhāri, Phālguṇa śu. 10, Monday Vyatipāta. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Refers to the kings rule over Koṅkaṇa-900, Palasige-1200, and Kavaḍadēva śavālakka and Vijayāditya's administration over anina kalpa bhūmi. Next his feudatory Bamma-gavuṇḍa, his son Māḍigavuṇḍa, and his son-in-law Kālaṅkāra-gavuṇḍa are praised for their noble deeds. Further, it registers a gift of land (the details are specified) on the date of the record to god Grāmēśvara for the worship and food offerings and also for aṅga-raṅga-bhōga, after obtaining the consent of the king by Bammagavuṇḍa. The gift was made after laving the feet of Ananta-śaktidēva, the āchārya of Kūḍala Hemmēśvara, on the holy occasion of solar-eclipse. Also records many more grants by various persons for the same god. In characters of about the 12th century A.D.

cells.location: Chāmarājanagara
cells.place: Stone Wode- fixed to the left side yars of wall of the mukha- maṇḍapa of Chaṁdrarājēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: States that the king established the town Chāmarājanagar and got constructed a temple of Kempaṁjamāṁbā- samēta Śrī Chāmarājēśvara, in his parents names established with enclosure, tower with golden pinnacles and also got installed the liṅga and goddess along with Chāmuṇḍēśvari on the right side of the main deity. Further states that to the eastern side a tower was erected and the southern side of the main deity the ancient idols were consecrated and the western side of the enclosure, a row of sahasa-lingas were installed and on the northern side stone enclosure the idols of pañchaviṁśati mūrtartis and on the north eastern corner a separate shrine of Lakshmīnārāyaṇa was constructed. Further it registers the grant of 13 villages (name specified) with all its imposts to god and an annual income of 4900 varāhas and 4 haṇas which was granted for various worship and ceremonies by the king. At the end, it also states that the idols of the kings with that of his chief queen and other queens were also got installed in the same temple complex. (Published in Ep. Carn. (Revised), Vol. IV, Ch. No. 5, pages. 9-10).

cells.remarks: States that as a result of a mutual understanding between Chandraśēkhara-Voḍeya, son of Channarāja-Voḍeya, the chief of Arekōthāra-sthala and Malarāja-voḍeya, son of Vīra-Rāmaya voḍeya of Kammaravalli the village Haṁgārepura, situated in Uyyamvalli-sthala of Ummattūrsīmā was made over to god Virabhadradeva of Arekōthāra as saramāṇya for offerings to god and the maintenance of dancing girls in the temple (pātra-bhōga). cells.location: Gundlupēte
cells.place: Lower part of the southern basement of the sanctum of Rāmēśvara temple. Base of the northern side of sanctuary of the same temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1294. Chaitra śu. 10, Monday 1372 A.D., March 15 (the cyclic year is lost)
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that the services of Kētavve, a dancing girl (pātra) in the temple of Rāmānātha of Vijayapura was offered by a certain Hiriyā-Rāmaṇṇa son of Nāgavve, and the vira-pānchālas, a body agreed to pay money for her maintenance. These vira-pānchālas were highly eulogised and were said to have been the lords of Piṇḍōtpura, the devotees of Kālīkādēvi and Kamatēśvara and hailed from several places like Terakaṇāmbe, the capital of the rāya (rāya-kaṭaka) and Kuḍugumāḍum Kōlugāna, Kāre-nāḍu, Hosav-nāḍu and several sthalas (names given). Further, it is stipulated that the carpenters, goldsmiths and braziers of every village should pay a fixed sum annually. (Published in Ep. Carn. (Revised), Vol. III, Gu. No. 17, p. 18 ff).

cells.place: Dō. Dō.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of 30 kalañju of gold by two members (names given) of the āluṇgaṇa-makkal of the place, to provide for the abhishēka of the deity Mūlasthānam-udaiyār of Vāgūr. It further states that puṇṇiya-gaṇattu-perumakkal had agreed to conduct the abhishēka by supplying water through lift on three sandhis, to the above deity. It is stipulated that in case of default of the gift a fine (maṇru-pāḍu) of one eighth for a poṇ -was to be paid and the abhishēka to be performed by the maṇruvār (court of justice). Dō.

cells.king: Seṇḍan-Māraṇ(i.e., Māraṇ, the son of Seṇḍan)
cells.remarks: Stone broken at the top. Probably two or three lines are missing in the beginning. cells.place:
Melur Taluk
Mēḷvalaivu.—A rocky outcrop known as Paramakamāmy, at the foot hills of Sōmagiri to the west of the village.
cells.dynasty: Sundara-Pāṇḍya, who took and gave Sōṇāḍu. (Mārvarmaṇ Sundara pāṇḍya I)
cells.king: Seṇḍan-Māraṇ(i.e., Māraṇ, the son of Seṇḍan)
cells.remarks: States that Āḷvāṇ Charkkarakkaiyāṇ of Kōvūr raised a stone channel over the rock and sluice (kaliṅgu) without endangering the embankment of the lake at Parambu alias Tirunārāyaṇamaṅgalam in Vaḍaparappu-nāḍu for the irrigation of the wet lands. The above village is referred to as a tiruvidaiyāṭṭam village of the deity Aḷagar (Kallagar temple). In characters of the 13th century A.D.

cells.place: (Iraṭṭai Chōla Tirupati), Dēvapiran temple, maṇḍapa, pillar,
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Registers the sale of lands by the ūrōm of Uttamaśālanallūr to the śrī-vaiṣṇavās of the eighteen maṇḍalas, after receiving the tax value (irai-dravyam). It was stipulated that the latter should supply paddy for the food offerings to be made on every Amāvāsya day to the deity Niṉṇaruḷiṇa-eṁberumāṉ of Tuḷavivilainagalam in Tiruvaluḍi-valanādu of Rājarāja-Pāṇḍi-nāḍu. It states that specified quantities of paddy have to be provided for the feeding of the various persons serving in the Pichchaṇ Māṇikkaṇmā maṭha, on the days of Amāvāsya. In characters of about the 11th century A.D.

cells.date: A.H. 1287 (& chronogram) = 1870 A.D., April 3 - 1871 A.D., March 22
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a mosque by Badru'd-Dīn 'Alī Khān. The text further states that of the whole property comprising landed property and agricultural field which he has endowed, he bequeathed its half portion to his descendants and the remaining half was to be utilised for the needy persons. It enjoins that the Muslims should not create trouble on this distribution. The chronogram was composed by Naqsh. Pub. in Waqā'i-i-Dārul-Ḥukūmat-i-Delhi, Vol. II, p. 213.

cells.date: (1) A.H. 886 (& chronogram), Ṣafar 5, (2) 1481 A.D., (April 5) (3) A.H. 1347 (& chronogram) (4) 1928 A.D.
cells.remarks: States that the headstone at the grave of Ḥadrat Makhdūm Jahāniyān, Amīrul-Umarā, Malik-ut-Tujjār, Khwāja-i-Jahān, 'Imādud-Dīn Maḥmūd Gāwān, the martyr (Shahīd), Wakīlus-Sultanat of the Bahmani kingdom of Muḥammadābād-Bīdar deccan who obtained martyrdom on the first date, was set up on the second date at the behest of Mahārāja Bahādur Yaminus-Sultanat Sir Kishan Parshād. It also records a chronogram of the martyrdom of Maḥmūd Gāwān which was composed by Mullā 'Abdul-Karīm Hamadānī, who is described as friend and biographer of the deceased Khwāja (Maḥmūd Gāwān).

cells.remarks: Damaged. States that the Jāmi‘ mosque was originally built on the first date by Sayyid Muḥammad Akram at the instance of Ankus Khān, had become old. Ind., Western Circle for the year ending 31st March 1921 (Bombay-1922), p. 57.
